target_snapshot.body: It may therefore well be said, with good reason, that the general study of language calls for considering the American languages in their interconnection, inquiring into and describing their structure, and comparing it with that of the languages of the other continents. My intention in the present work is to do this to the best of my abilities, with due completeness, but above all through inquiry that penetrates as deeply as possible into the essential character of these languages. To achieve this aim, I have for a number of years not merely studied the individual languages but also prepared my own treatments of them, and for an even longer time collected materials, chiefly in manuscript. Collecting of this kind can never attain completeness; that is inherent in the nature of the matter itself. But the resources that are at my disposal and are to be regarded as sources for this investigation provide, when combined with what has already been very usefully prepared in several other works, abundant material for a treatment covering the whole field of this investigation, and sufficient material for a reliable assessment.
